authority: Bounded monitor-escalation source review and existing tests with subprocess test doubles
reviewedBehavior: Escalation is configured for detached converging monitor policy; without an injected seam, it also requires detached-job attribution.
The monitor loads a new PR wave after inbox convergence, excluding row IDs and red-set keys it has already settled.
Only spawned or already-escalated outcomes update the loop settlement state; owner-live and spawn-failed outcomes remain eligible for a later poll.
Notifier ownership resolution reads the PR-session registry and configured owner-process/session probes. Unresolved repository or unreadable registry returns a non-live verdict.
A non-live-owner wave claims its descriptor exclusively before launching the worker. A failed launch removes the claim so a later attempt can retry.
semanticInputs: Attachment mode, monitor policy and detached-job environment attribution
PR number, observed head, URL, wave rows and red-set identity
Persisted claims, worker-file existence and current clock
Session registry, HOME-derived session directory and process-probe state
Per-loop sets of previously escalated row IDs and red-set keys
effects: Writes claim/descriptor files and removes claims after failed launch
Can launch a detached worker through setsid and emit console messages in production; the tests replace subprocess execution
limits: No real notifier worker, desktop notification or owner-session action was launched for this review.
Launch success and existing claims do not prove worker completion, notification delivery or human acknowledgement.
Complete registry/probe internals, crash recovery and concurrent-claim semantics remain outside this review.
The operation depends on fresh external and mutable local state; it is not qualified for task-result replay.
